title: Microsoft Intune: Windows quality update policies with per-type approval (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates which .NET Framework updates the approval policy controls, omitting the exclusion of .NET Framework 3.5. It also describes eight hours as an upper bound for resume instructions, whereas Microsoft describes that communication interval as an average. The roadmap facts, licensing requirements and principal controls are otherwise supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents these policies although the roadmap still says In development.
claims.quote: Windows quality update policies allow you to manage Windows quality updates and supported .NET Framework updates for Windows devices.

claims.claim: Administrators configure automatic or manual approval independently by Windows quality update type.
claims.quote: You can configure an approval method for Windows quality updates by individual update type. A single policy can use both automatic and manual methods across different update types.

claims.claim: The documented update types are monthly security, monthly non-security preview, out-of-band security and out-of-band non-security.
claims.quote: Monthly security updates; Monthly non-security preview updates; Out-of-band (OOB) security updates; Out-of-band non-security updates

claims.claim: The settings apply to both the Windows OS update and the .NET Framework update of each type without a Framework-version qualification.
claims.quote: You can't manage .NET Framework 3.5 updates through Windows Autopatch quality update policies. These updates don't appear in the quality updates workflow. Windows Update delivers these updates as standalone. Client-side settings govern these updates.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The settings apply to Windows OS updates and supported .NET Framework updates of that type on Windows 11; .NET Framework 3.5 updates remain governed by client-side settings.' Keep the existing Windows 10 ESU qualification in Scope. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/deployment/windows-autopatch/manage/windows-autopatch-windows-quality-update-overview.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A newly created policy defaults monthly security updates to automatic approval.
claims.quote: When you create a quality update policy, the default approval configuration of monthly security updates is automatic.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Other update types, including out-of-band security updates, default to manual approval.
claims.quote: The default approval configuration of other updates is manual.

claims.claim: The deferral period applies to automatically approved updates.
claims.quote: Deferral periods only apply to automatically approved updates. For manual approval, you control when updates are offered by approving policies at your chosen time.

claims.claim: The allowed quality update deferral range is 0 to 30 days.
claims.quote: The allowed range is 0 to 30 days for quality updates.

claims.claim: The automatic deferral setting is named Make updates available after.
claims.quote: If you choose automatic approval, select Make updates available after. Specify the number of days to wait before updates are offered to devices.

claims.claim: Manage updates lets an administrator inspect a release's severity and included KBs before approving it for selected policies.
claims.quote: Select a Release name to see details, such as severity and included KBs. Use this information to review the payload before manual approval.

claims.claim: An approved quality update release can be paused.
claims.quote: You can pause an approved update at any time.

claims.claim: Pausing does not roll back devices that already installed the update.
claims.quote: Devices that already installed the update aren't rolled back.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: This new approval control is admin-opt-in: devices without a quality update policy keep standard Windows Update behaviour.
claims.quote: You don't need to create a Windows quality update policy for devices to continue receiving monthly Windows quality updates. Devices without a quality update policy continue to receive quality updates through standard Windows Update behavior

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a change caused by this approval capability for tenants that do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Windows quality update policies no policy default approval. Opened Manage Windows quality updates, Windows update management overview, and Windows quality updates and .NET Framework updates; none states this approval control changes unassigned devices.

claims.claim: An assigned policy governs approval, so a manually governed update is not deployed without approval.
claims.quote: When a device is assigned to a policy, it is enrolled in Autopatch for that content type, and only approved content is deployed to that device.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends automatic approval for security updates.
claims.quote: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approvals for security updates and manual approvals for optional updates.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends manual approval for optional or non-security updates.
claims.quote: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approvals for security updates and manual approvals for optional updates. Manual approval: Recommended for optional or non-security updates in special cases.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that timely approval of critical updates is essential to security compliance.
claims.quote: Use this setting with care, since timely approval of critical updates is essential to maintain security compliance.

claims.claim: No new organisational data category is described for this approval capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Windows quality update policies collected data privacy organizational data. Opened feature overview, Manage Windows quality updates, Windows update management overview and Autopatch Privacy; found existing policy, device and diagnostic data, not a new category for approvals.

claims.claim: Intune stores policy assignments rather than the updates themselves.
claims.quote: Intune stores only the policy assignments, not the updates themselves.

claims.claim: Intune sends configuration details to Windows Autopatch, which determines update approval.
claims.quote: When you save a policy, Intune sends configuration details to Windows Autopatch, which determines which updates are approved for deployment.

claims.claim: Devices download approved updates from Windows Update.
claims.quote: Devices download approved updates directly from Windows Update

claims.claim: Reporting requires allowing Intune access to Windows diagnostic data from enrolled devices.
claims.quote: To enable reporting for this feature, ensure your organization allows Intune to access Windows diagnostic data collected from enrolled devices.

claims.claim: Devices need Windows diagnostic data enabled at the Required level.
claims.quote: Telemetry must be turned on, with a minimum setting of Required.

claims.claim: Pausing revokes approval and prevents new devices from receiving that release.
claims.quote: When paused, Windows Autopatch revokes the approval of the update, and no new devices receive it.

claims.claim: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new pause settings.
claims.quote: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new update pause settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft states that resume instructions take up to eight hours to apply.
claims.quote: Windows devices take on average eight hours to communicate back to Microsoft Intune with new instructions to pause, resume, or roll back updates.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft says devices can take up to eight hours to apply a pause or resume' with 'Microsoft says devices can take up to eight hours to apply new pause settings; communication with Intune for pause or resume instructions takes eight hours on average.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/deployment/windows-autopatch/manage/windows-autopatch-windows-quality-update-overview.

claims.quote: | Autopatch Administrator | No permission |

claims.quote: Automatic approval: Recommended for security updates. Updates are auto-approved and deployed according to configured schedule, reducing administrative effort.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cloud-based quality policy deferral overrides update-ring or CSP client-side deferral.
claims.quote: Deferral periods set in cloud-based quality update policies override any client-side deferral settings from legacy update ring policies or CSP configurations.

claims.claim: Assigning a device to a quality update policy automatically enrolls it in Autopatch for that content type.
claims.quote: When a device is assigned to a policy, it is enrolled in Autopatch for that content type

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: After removal from every quality update policy, a device remains enrolled for 24 hours.
claims.quote: When a device is no longer assigned to any quality update policies, the device remains enrolled in Windows Autopatch for 24 hours.

claims.claim: After that interval, the device is unenrolled for quality updates and resumes Windows Update scans and client settings.
claims.quote: After 24 hours, the device is automatically unenrolled from Windows Autopatch for quality updates. From then on, the device receives updates based on Windows Update scans and client settings.

claims.claim: An existing quality update policy's approval method cannot be edited.
claims.quote: No, you can't change the approval method in an existing policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft says to create a new policy when a different approval method is needed.
claims.quote: If you need a different approval method, create a new policy.

claims.claim: A policy with hotpatch enabled does not deliver approved non-security updates to its devices.
claims.quote: If a policy has hotpatch updates enabled and non-security updates are approved, will the device receive the non-security updates? No, the devices won't receive non-security updates in this case.

claims.claim: Microsoft says to disable the policy's hotpatch setting to receive non-security updates.
claims.quote: To receive non-security updates, disable the hotpatch update setting in the quality update policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Among multiple cloud-based quality update policies, the policy approving the latest release takes priority.
claims.quote: Device assigned to multiple cloud-based quality update policies. The policy approving the latest release takes priority.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A cloud-based quality policy takes priority over a legacy quality policy containing only hotpatch settings.
claims.quote: Device assigned to cloud-based quality update policy and legacy quality update policy (with only the hotpatch update setting). The cloud-based quality update policy takes priority.

claims.claim: In that legacy-policy conflict, monthly security updates are not offered until approved manually or automatically.
claims.quote: That is, monthly security updates aren't offered to the device until you either manually or automatically approve them.
